tier_reason: No speed numbers on any opened page. The only comparative statement is directional: the MRI-NUFFT JOSS paper source (docs/paper-joss/paper.md) says that, per its benchmark, cufinufft and gpuNUFFT provide the best performances by leveraging CUDA acceleration. matlab/demo/run_demo.m times gpuNUFFT against a CPU NUFFT operator but publishes no results.

corrections.baseline: CPU NUFFT libraries (FINUFFT, pyNFFT, BART, SigPy, TorchKbNufft) as compared in the MRI-NUFFT benchmark; directional statement only, no numbers published
corrections.claimed_speedup: No numbers. Directional only: the MRI-NUFFT JOSS paper source says 'Using our benchmark ... At the time of writing, cufinufft and gpuNUFFT provide the best performances by leveraging CUDA acceleration'; MRI-NUFFT docs (backend.rst) recommend finufft for CPU and cufinufft or gpunufft when a CUDA GPU is available.
corrections.stars_or_usage: 85 stars, 37 forks; a gpuNUFFT backend of MRI-NUFFT (JOSS) and pysap-mri; the actively maintained fork chaithyagr/gpuNUFFT is what PyPI gpuNUFFT ships (0.10.8, released 2026-07-08)
corrections.caveats: Tier D: no speed numbers anywhere I could open. README gives install steps only (tested with CUDA 5.0 and gcc 4.6; a 2022 merge adds CUDA 11 support). matlab/demo/run_demo.m and cgsense_phantom_recon_cpu.m time gpuNUFFT forward/adjoint against a CPU NUFFT operator with tic/toc, but no results are committed. The LICENSE cites Knoll et al., Proc ISMRM 2014 p4297 (conference abstract, not opened) and README points to Dropbox 'Supporting material' (not opened). mind-inria/mri-nufft-benchmark commits no results; the MRI-NUFFT JOSS paper source (docs/paper-joss/paper.md in mind-inria/mri-nufft, opened via raw.githubusercontent.com) states only that cufinufft and gpuNUFFT give the best performance in that benchmark, with no numbers; its authors include the gpuNUFFT Python-binding author (Chaithya G R), so it is not fully independent. Published third-party comparisons (for example the cuFINUFFT paper) were not checked; the direction against cuFINUFFT is unknown to me. The upstream repo's last commit is 2022-02-06 (abandoned), but MRI-NUFFT docs name chaithyagr/gpuNUFFT (a GitHub fork, 2 stars, 1,356 commits) as the active fork and PyPI gpuNUFFT 0.10.8 was released 2026-07-08. LICENSE is MIT plus a request to credit the authors and cite the ISMRM abstract in academic work. Baselines FFTW, MKL FFT and KissFFT in the assignment are not what gpuNUFFT is compared with; the relevant incumbents are CPU NUFFTs.

notes: Confirmed D; not rejected because it is a used, cited MRI backend (MRI-NUFFT, pysap-mri, ISMRM 2014) with an independent-ish directional claim in the MRI-NUFFT JOSS paper. Consider pointing the entry, or a note, at the active fork chaithyagr/gpuNUFFT that PyPI ships.

tier_reason: No numbers and no comparison against FFTW, MKL or cuFFT in the README, docs/source/details.rst, index.rst or tests/programs/benchmark.cpp (which times only SpFFT transforms); not even a directional speed claim, so D.

corrections.baseline: FFTW / MKL and cuFFT / rocFFT dense 3D FFT (implied; no comparison is published; SpFFT itself calls these libraries for its 1D/2D sub-transforms)
corrections.stars_or_usage: 56 stars, 16 forks; conda-forge package; listed as a required dependency ('domain-specific FFT library') in the SIRIUS README, the electronic-structure library used by Quantum ESPRESSO and CP2K
corrections.caveats: Tier D: no numeric comparison against any recognizable baseline and no stated speed claim. tests/programs/benchmark.cpp (CLI11 plus rt_graph timing, JSON output) runs only SpFFT transforms, with no FFTW, cuFFT or dense reference; README and docs/source/details.rst state no speed numbers. details.rst says the underlying computation is done by FFT libraries such as FFTW and cuFFT, so SpFFT is a sparse-aware decomposition layer on top of the baseline, not a replacement kernel; any gain comes from skipping work on empty z-columns and planes plus its MPI exchange schemes. Published performance data, if any (for example SIRIUS papers), is behind egress-blocked hosts (readthedocs, doi.org, arXiv) and was not checked. Notability: 56 stars, but SIRIUS lists it as a required dependency (verified in the SIRIUS README). The latest commit, 'fix array size mismatch for local transforms (#65)' on 2025-07-25, comes after the last release v1.1.1 (2025-01-19); the PR has no description, so whether released builds can mis-size buffers for local transforms is unknown. Last commit date read from the github.com commits page.

notes: Confirmed D with no speed claim at all; kept rather than rejected because it is a required dependency of SIRIUS (QE/CP2K backend). Shortcoming worth recording: unreleased post-v1.1.1 fix for an array size mismatch in local transforms (#65).
